attempts.summary: Configured dynamic route exchange between node1 and node2 (SONiC switches) via iBGP (AS 65100) over their transit link, so each learns the other's private network without static routes. node1's private subnet 192.168.13.0/24 (to node3) and node2's private subnet 192.168.24.0/24 (to node4) are advertised via BGP `network` statements over a /31 transit link (172.20.1.0/172.20.1.1 on eth1↔eth1), and each side installs the peer's subnet in its kernel FIB with `proto bgp`. node3 and node4 gained only a static route to their own gateway router (unavoidable for non-BGP-speaking end hosts) and can now ping each other end-to-end. All config was made boot-persistent (SONiC regenerates FRR config from configdb at boot, wiping raw edits, so a companion systemd unit reapplies BGP peering after container start). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with boot-id proof and post-restart recovery proof; node1 and node2 (SONiC-VS) each took ~14 minutes to fully recover after `shutdown -r now`.
